names_aka: ENEPIG (electroless Ni / electroless Pd / immersion Au) — stack variant
'liquid gold dip' (hobby marketing term for immersion gold)
principle: Two distinct chemistries, no rectifier in either. (1) IMMERSION (displacement) gold: the workpiece's own surface metal is the reducing agent — less-noble metal (Ni from an electroless Ni-P underlayer, or Cu/Ag) dissolves while Au(I) from solution plates in its place (Ni0 + 2Au(I) -> Ni2+ + 2Au0). The reaction is SELF-LIMITING: once gold covers the surface the electron source is cut off and deposition stops — hence a hard thickness ceiling around 0.05-0.15 um [FACT: mechanism + published ceiling]. (2) AUTOCATALYTIC (true electroless) gold: a chemical reducing agent in the bath (borohydride, DMAB, hydrazine, ascorbate/thiourea in cyanide-free systems) reduces Au(I) on a catalytically active gold surface, so deposition continues indefinitely — thickness limited only by bath control, practically 0.3-2+ um. Both ride on ELECTROLESS NICKEL-PHOSPHORUS (hypophosphite-reduced autocatalytic Ni-P alloy) as the standard underlayer/barrier, whose defining virtue is PERFECTLY UNIFORM thickness on any shape — no current distribution, no edge build-up, coats bores/recesses/complex geometry identically [FACT: mechanism].

substrates: steel and stainless steel (EN Ni-P initiates directly on activated steel — steel is catalytic to hypophosphite baths)
copper/brass (need Pd catalyzation or galvanic initiation nudge for EN; immersion Au deposits directly on Cu but embrittles solder joints — electronics lore, less relevant here)
NON-CONDUCTORS: glass, ceramic, plastic — via sensitize/activate (SnCl2 then PdCl2, or mixed Sn-Pd colloid) then electroless Ni or Cu seed [FACT: standard metallization route]
complex shapes, internal surfaces, chain, filigree, hollow ware — the geometry class where electroplating throwing power fails
applicability.steel_wire_notes: EN Ni-P coats wire perfectly uniformly with zero rectifier and zero bipolar/shielding issues — attractive for coils and tangled batches. BUT: (a) the immersion-gold top layer is capped at ~0.1 um — flash class only, far below jewelry wear thickness; (b) Ni-P is HARD AND BRITTLE (see deposit_properties) — the ENIG stack is the WORST possible choice for plate-then-form wire: Ni-P cracks/crazes at small bend radii and takes the gold with it [FACT: Ni-P low ductility is published]. Honest position for the anchor product: ENIG is NOT the route to gold-plated steel-wire rings as a final finish; its real jewelry-adjacent role is (1) uniform Ni barrier on complex/hollow steel pieces that then get ELECTROplated gold on top, (2) gold flash on low-wear decorative items, (3) the metallization front-end for non-conductive houseware.
applicability.non_conductive_notes: THIS is where the family earns its place in the owner's portfolio: glass cups, ceramic ware, plastic parts cannot be electroplated directly, but sensitize (SnCl2/HCl) -> activate (PdCl2 or Sn-Pd colloid) -> electroless Ni-P (or electroless Cu) gives a conductive, adherent metal skin over the whole object — after which ANY electroplating route (incl. the sibling gold files) applies [FACT: standard practice, decorative 'plating on plastics/glass' industry]. Mirror-silvering (Tollens) is the classical alternative seed for glass. Food-contact: Ni-P release, Pb-stabilized EN baths and gold-bath residues on drinkware are a regulatory minefield — [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check per market]; EN 1811 Ni-release applies to skin-contact jewelry with Ni-P exposed or near-exposed [FACT: regulation exists].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: Immersion gold: 0.04-0.15 um — BELOW even the 'flash' decorative class floor (0.05-0.175 um), color-only, near-zero wear life. IPC-4552 (the ENIG standard, electronics) specifies immersion Au ~0.04-0.1 um class over 3-6 um EN [FACT: published class]. Autocatalytic gold extends to 0.3-2 um — reaching 'gold plated' (>=0.5 um) and low-micron class, used in electronics (ENIG + autocatalytic build = 'electrolytic-free thick gold') but slow and expensive per um. ISO 27874 jewelry classes technically apply to the gold layer regardless of how it was deposited.

components.name: electroless Ni tank + precision heater
components.purpose: hold EN bath at 85-91 C +/-1-2 C — rate and P-content are steep functions of T
components.diy_notes: glass/PP-rated-hot/stainless-with-liner; NEVER plain uncoated stainless or mild steel tank — the bath plates the tank (it's catalytic!); industry uses passivated tanks with periodic nitric strip-out, DIY uses glass or disposable PP liners. Water-bath (bain-marie) heating gives DIY the needed stability and avoids hot-spot decomposition on heater surfaces.

components.name: immersion / electroless gold tank + heater
components.purpose: hold gold bath at its 60-90 C window
components.diy_notes: small (0.5-2 L) lidded glass/PP vessel — gold inventory logic says keep this bath tiny; same water-bath heating trick.

components.name: NO RECTIFIER
components.purpose: the family's defining hardware absence — deposition is chemical, not electrolytic
components.diy_notes: removes the power supply, anodes, contact racks, bipolar worries, and burned-edge failure mode entirely; this is the whole hardware pitch.

components.name: plastic baskets / hooks / tumbling fixtures
components.purpose: hold parts with full solution access; no electrical contact needed
components.diy_notes: PP mesh baskets work — parts can even touch lightly (no contact-point shadow like electroplating); gentle motion prevents gas-pit streaks (H2 evolves during EN).

components.name: thermometer + pH meter
components.purpose: EN rate/quality lives on T and pH; immersion Au on T, pH and time
components.diy_notes: calibrated pH meter mandatory; EN pH drifts DOWN in use (H+ generated) — correct with dilute ammonia per TDS.

components.name: loading-factor discipline (not hardware)
components.purpose: EN baths need surface-area-to-volume in window (~0.5-1.5 dm2/L class) — too low: bath destabilizes/plates out; too high: rate crashes, dark deposits
components.diy_notes: count your cm2 before dipping; this replaces the ammeter of electroplating as the 'dose' control [FACT: standard EN practice].

components.name: continuous/periodic filtration 1-5 um
components.purpose: EN baths are metastable — any particle (dust, Ni fines) seeds spontaneous bath-wide decomposition ('bath crash': the whole tank plates out as black sponge in minutes)
components.diy_notes: filter EN religiously; a crashed EN bath is unrecoverable and coats everything it touched.

components.name: sensitize/activate line for non-conductors (SnCl2 dip, PdCl2 or colloidal Sn-Pd dip)
components.purpose: seed catalytic Pd sites on glass/ceramic/plastic so EN can initiate
components.diy_notes: small beakers; PdCl2 is the expensive drop; commercial 'plating on plastic' activator kits exist; surface must be etched/roughened first (glass: HF-etch class or sandblast — HF is a hard NO for DIY, use mechanical/plasma roughening or commercial no-HF etchants).

components.name: drag-out + rinse tanks
components.purpose: gold economy on the Au tank; Ni-P and activator carry-over control between stages
components.diy_notes: Pd activator dragged into the EN bath is a decomposition trigger; rinse well after activation.

components.name: MTO (metal-turnover) log
components.purpose: EN baths AGE by orthophosphite accumulation — usable life ~4-8 metal turnovers, then dump/replace [FACT: standard EN limitation]
components.diy_notes: a notebook, not a device: track g of Ni replenished vs initial bath Ni; past MTO limit deposits go dull, stressed, slow.

operation_sequence.action: verify EN bath: temperature, pH, Ni and hypophosphite in range (test kit/titration), filtered, no plate-out specks on tank; verify gold bath T/pH
operation_sequence.parameters: EN 85-91 C, pH 4.4-5.2 (mid-phos class); immersion Au 75-90 C, pH per TDS (4.5-7 class)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: grey film or gas streamers on tank wall = incipient EN decomposition — filter, drop T, or dump before it cascades

operation_sequence.action: pretreat substrate: degrease -> (metal: electroclean/pickle; stainless: Wood's strike or proprietary activator; non-conductor: etch -> SnCl2 sensitize -> PdCl2 activate)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skip plating (bald patches) = activation failure or grease; steel flash-rusting between steps = re-pickle

operation_sequence.action: immerse in electroless Ni-P; parts hang/lie in basket, gentle agitation or periodic rocking
operation_sequence.parameters: 85-91 C, pH 4.4-5.2, loading 0.5-1.5 dm2/L, deposition ~12-20 um/h mid-phos [FACT: published typical range]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: H2 gas pits on upward-facing surfaces (rock the parts); edge-to-center thickness is UNIFORM — if it is not, the bath, not the geometry, is sick; dark/dull = pH low, T low, or bath past MTO

operation_sequence.action: rinse thoroughly (DI), transfer WET and promptly to gold — fresh Ni-P passivates in air within minutes like any nickel
operation_sequence.failure_watch: delayed transfer = passive Ni = thin/patchy immersion gold and adhesion loss

operation_sequence.action: immersion gold dip: displacement reaction runs, visibly gilding the surface, then self-terminates
operation_sequence.parameters: 75-90 C, pH 4.5-7 class, Au 0.5-2 g/L; time 5-15 min to plateau
operation_sequence.duration: 5-15 min — LONGER BUYS ALMOST NOTHING past plateau, and over-dwell corrodes the Ni underneath (black pad mechanism)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: over-long dwell / hyperactive bath = black-pad class hyper-corrosion of Ni-P grain boundaries under the gold — gold looks fine, stack is rotten [FACT: the canonical ENIG failure]

operation_sequence.action: OPTIONAL thickness build: transfer to autocatalytic electroless gold bath (reduction-type) to grow 0.3-2 um on top of the immersion flash
operation_sequence.parameters: 60-80 C, rate ~1-3 um/h [FACT: published class range]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: autocatalytic Au baths are the least stable baths in this file — spontaneous plate-out on tank/dust; keep small, filtered, lidded

operation_sequence.action: cascade rinse (recover first rinse to drag-out), hot DI final rinse, warm-air dry
operation_sequence.failure_watch: staining in recesses — the same complex geometry that plated uniformly also traps rinse water; blow out bores

operation_sequence.action: inspect + test per testing_acceptance; log MTO on the EN bath
operation_sequence.parameters: XRF Au and Ni thickness, color, adhesion coupon
operation_sequence.failure_watch: pale/ghostly gold color = immersion layer under ~0.05 um (bath Au low, T low, or passive Ni) — do not ship as 'gold plated'

solutions.solution_name: electroless nickel-phosphorus, mid-phosphorus acid hypophosphite bath (the underlayer workhorse)
solutions.purpose: autocatalytic Ni-P (6-9 wt% P) barrier/leveler: perfectly uniform, hard, corrosion-blocking underlayer on any shape; the 'EN' of ENIG

composition.hazard_class: Carc. 2 / STOT / skin sensitizer Cat 1 (the #1 contact allergen), aquatic-toxic [FACT]

composition.role: reducing agent AND phosphorus source (co-deposits 6-9% P); oxidizes to orthophosphite which accumulates and ends bath life
composition.hazard_class: low hazard solid; evolves phosphine only on strong heating/contact with strong oxidizers [FACT]

composition.chemical: complexants: lactic acid + propionic/acetic or citrate/glycolate blends
composition.role: hold Ni2+ soluble, buffer pH, control free-Ni activity and thus rate/stability

composition.chemical: stabilizer: Pb2+ (classic) or S-compounds (thiourea class) or newer Pb-free (Bi, Sb, iodate)
composition.role: poison stray catalytic nuclei so the bath deposits ONLY on the work — the knife-edge between bath crash (too little) and edge skip-plating/no initiation (too much)
composition.hazard_class: lead compounds: Repr. 1A, cumulative toxin — Pb-stabilized EN is a food-contact disqualifier; Pb-free EN products exist and should be preferred [FACT]

composition.role: pH drifts acid in use (H+ byproduct) — ammonia feed is routine

operating_window.temperature_C: 85-91 (rate roughly halves per ~10 C drop; below ~80 C mid-phos barely deposits) [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.pH: 4.4-5.2 acid hypophosphite class; higher pH = faster + lower P; lower pH = slower + higher P [FACT: published relationship]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: n/a — chemical deposition; the analogous dose control is LOADING FACTOR 0.5-1.5 dm2/L [FACT: standard practice]
operating_window.agitation: gentle solution movement / part rocking to shed H2 bubbles; no air blasting needed
operating_window.deposition_rate: 12-20 um/h mid-phos at 88-90 C — i.e. ~3-5 min per micron, but you take the whole-bath uniformity, not a rate you can crank [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.anode: none — hypophosphite is the electron source; Ni replenished as concentrate (Ni + hypo + stabilizer paired feeds per TDS)

solutions.maintenance: Analyze/replenish Ni2+ (keep +/-10% of setpoint) and hypophosphite (molar ratio hypo:Ni ~3-4:1 class); correct pH up with dilute ammonia. Log METAL TURNOVERS: orthophosphite accumulates ~as much as Ni deposited; at 4-8 MTO deposits dull, stress rises, rate falls — dump and remake, this is a scheduled consumable [FACT: standard EN limitation]. Filter 1-5 um continuously; strip any plate-out from tank with nitric between makeups. Contamination: Pd drag-in from activators = crash trigger; Zn, Pb excess = skip plating; sulfide = black deposits [ESTIMATE: handbook-class limits, exact ppm per TDS].

solutions.solution_name: immersion gold (displacement), cyanide-complex acid type (ENIG gold)
solutions.purpose: self-limiting 0.04-0.15 um gold flash over Ni-P by galvanic exchange — color, solderability (electronics), oxidation seal; the 'IG' of ENIG

composition.role: gold source; very stable complex (log beta ~38) — at mildly acidic pH the complex holds, free cyanide is essentially nil BUT acid contact rules still apply
composition.hazard_class: acutely toxic (cyanide salt, H300/H310/H330 class); mixing with strong acid liberates HCN [FACT]

composition.chemical: chelators/buffer: citrate, phosphate, or organic-acid blends + EDTA-class Ni sequestrant
composition.role: buffer the 4.5-7 window; sequester the Ni2+ that the displacement reaction pumps into the bath (Ni tolerance defines bath life)

composition.chemical: rate/corrosion moderators (proprietary): inhibit Ni-P grain-boundary attack (anti-black-pad package)
composition.role: the quality heart of modern ENIG gold: slow the displacement to a controlled, shallow exchange instead of pitting corrosion

operating_window.pH: 4.5-7 class (product-specific; 'neutral' immersion golds sit 6-7 and corrode Ni less) [FACT: published class]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: n/a — driven by the Ni/Au exchange potential
operating_window.agitation: gentle; excessive agitation accelerates Ni corrosion locally
operating_window.deposition_rate: 0.05-0.1 um in 5-15 min, then SELF-TERMINATES — the thickness CEILING is the mechanism, not a settings choice; doubling time does not double thickness [FACT: mechanism + published]
operating_window.anode: none; Au replenished as KAu(CN)2 salt/concentrate; bath retires when dissolved Ni exceeds tolerance (g/L class per TDS)

solutions.maintenance: Track Au (feed to setpoint) and accumulated Ni2+ — Ni is the death clock of an immersion gold bath (typ. tolerance a few g/L class [ESTIMATE: handbook, medium]); pH drift corrected per TDS. Never let strong acid near it (cyanide complex). Carry-over of EN bath into gold accelerates Ni load — good rinse before gold extends bath life directly. Dump-to-reclaimer at end of life: still gold-rich.

solutions.purpose: same displacement (and mixed displacement-autocatalytic) function without cyanide — the home-shop-compatible variant; also the standard seed-gold on metallized non-conductors in cyanide-free lines

composition.chemical: gold as sulfite and/or thiosulfate complex
composition.role: gold source; thiosulfate (log beta ~26) gives workable stability near-neutral pH
composition.hazard_class: low acute toxicity (no cyanide); SO2 evolution on acid contact [FACT]

composition.chemical: sodium sulfite + sodium thiosulfate ligand excess
composition.role: ligand pool + antioxidant; suppresses disproportionation and sulfur breakdown

composition.chemical: mild reducing/assist agent in 'assisted' versions (ascorbic acid, thiourea class)
composition.role: adds an autocatalytic component so deposition does not fully stop at displacement ceiling ('mixed-mode' baths reach 0.2-0.5 um)
composition.hazard_class: thiourea: Carc. 2 class; ascorbate low hazard [FACT: class-level]

operating_window.deposition_rate: displacement plateau 0.05-0.1 um in 10-20 min; mixed-mode versions crawl on to 0.2-0.5 um [ESTIMATE: published class, medium]
operating_window.anode: none; replenish Au salt; ligand oxidation and Ni load both age the bath — shorter life than cyanide-type immersion gold [FACT: recognized trade-off]

solutions.maintenance: Same Ni-accumulation death clock plus sulfite-family fragility: keep lidded, never acidify (SO2 + gold crash), filter fines. Realistically bought as a commercial product with paired replenisher; self-compounding not advised.

solutions.purpose: grow gold BEYOND the displacement ceiling with a chemical reducer: 0.3-2+ um uniform gold on any shape with no rectifier; classic system is the borohydride/cyanide 'Okinaka-type' bath, modern cyanide-free versions use sulfite/thiosulfate + ascorbate or hydrazine-class reducers

composition.hazard_class: cyanide type: acutely toxic; classic bath ALSO carries FREE KCN — the most cyanide-hazardous bath in this whole file family; CN-free type: low acute toxicity [FACT]

composition.chemical: free complexant (classic: KCN; CN-free: sulfite/thiosulfate excess)
composition.role: hold Au(I) speciation, prevent spontaneous reduction in bulk
composition.hazard_class: KCN: acutely toxic, HCN on acid [FACT]

composition.chemical: reducing agent: potassium borohydride or dimethylamine borane (DMAB); CN-free: ascorbate/hydrazine-class
composition.role: the electron source enabling unlimited thickness — and the instability source: it reduces Au anywhere, not just on the part
composition.hazard_class: borohydrides: water-reactive, evolve H2, corrosive; DMAB: acutely toxic class; hydrazine: Carc. 1B class [FACT]

composition.role: borohydride only survives at high pH

operating_window.pH: ~13 (borohydride/KCN classic); 6-9 for DMAB and CN-free types per TDS [FACT: published class]
operating_window.deposition_rate: 1-3 um/h class — an order of magnitude slower per um than electroplating; this is the price of rectifier-free thickness [FACT: published class range]
operating_window.anode: none; paired Au + reducer feeds per TDS; bath life short (reducer self-decomposes; plate-out on any nucleus)

solutions.maintenance: The fussiest bath in the family: reducer decomposes on standing (feed on schedule, not on analysis lag), any particle or scratch nucleates plate-out, tank walls gild themselves. Keep the bath SMALL, lidded, filtered, and accept short life. The classic KCN/borohydride version does not belong in a residential shop [FACT-adjacent judgment from hazard classes]; if the thickness-without-rectifier capability is truly needed, use a commercial CN-free reduction gold and follow its TDS exactly.

prep_chain_required: 1. Degrease (solvent/ultrasonic alkaline) — universal; EN skip-plates on any organic film.

2. METALS: alkaline electroclean or hot soak -> rinse -> acid pickle (mild steel: 10-30 vol% HCl) — active bare metal; stainless additionally needs Wood's Ni strike or a proprietary EN-on-stainless activation, else no initiation on the passive film [FACT].

3. NON-CONDUCTORS: surface roughening (mechanical/blast or commercial etch; classical chromic/HF etches are DIY-prohibited) -> SnCl2/HCl sensitize -> rinse -> PdCl2 activate (or one-step Sn-Pd colloid + accelerator) — deposits catalytic Pd nuclei so EN can start; WHY: EN needs a catalytic surface, glass/ceramic have none [FACT: standard metallization chain].
4. Rinse well after activation — Pd drag-in destabilizes the EN bath (crash trigger).

5. Electroless Ni-P 3-8 um — the uniform barrier/leveler; WHY: blocks Fe (or seals the Pd/seed), provides the sacrificial-donor surface the immersion gold reaction consumes; thickness matters because immersion gold eats ~the top tens of nm of it.
6. Prompt wet transfer to immersion gold (fresh, unpassivated Ni-P) — minutes matter.
7. Optional: autocatalytic gold build on top of the immersion flash (immersion layer doubles as the catalytic seed).

8. Optional hybrid (often the SMART route for jewelry): stop after EN or after immersion flash and switch to ELECTROplated gold from the sibling files for real decorative thickness — the part is now conductive and uniformly barriered regardless of original substrate or geometry.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: immersion and autocatalytic gold: 99.9%+ Au, 24k class, soft (ASTM B488 Type III class analog) — no hardened variants in common electroless practice [FACT: published characteristic]. Underlayer is Ni-P ALLOY (91-94% Ni, 6-9% P mid-phos), amorphous-to-microcrystalline.
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: gold layer: soft, ~60-90 HV class (and at 0.1 um, hardness is academic — the substrate reads through). Ni-P underlayer: 500-600 HV as-plated, 850-1000 HV after 400 C/1 h precipitation hardening [FACT: published typical values] — the STACK feels hard and scratch-resistant because Ni-P carries the load under a decorative gold skin; this is a genuine premium-feel trick IF gold thickness is honest about being flash.
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: immersion: 0.04-0.15 um HARD CEILING (self-limiting displacement) [FACT]; mixed-mode CN-free: to ~0.2-0.5 um; autocatalytic: 0.3-2+ um at 1-3 um/h. EN underlayer: any thickness, typically 3-25 um, perfectly uniform on any geometry.
deposit_properties.color_control: pure-gold rich yellow, but at immersion thickness (<0.1 um) the color is slightly muted/paled by the Ni-P beneath — visibly 'thinner' looking than 0.5+ um electroplate; autocatalytic build restores full-body gold color. No alloy-color options (rose/green) in standard electroless practice.
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: THE PLATE-THEN-FORM ANSWER FOR THIS FAMILY: NO — the worst of all routes. Ni-P is hard and near-zero-ductility (elongation ~1% class as-plated [FACT: published]); bending ENIG-coated wire cracks the Ni-P layer through-thickness, the crack network cuts the gold, and exposed Ni-P/steel then corrodes preferentially (gold is cathodic). Heat-forming makes it worse (hardening + embrittlement above ~300-400 C, plus Ni-Au interdiffusion discolors the flash). Form the wire/part FIRST — which is actually where this family shines, since finished complex shapes coat uniformly with no current-distribution penalty.

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class; IPC-4552 class values for ENIG stacks (Au ~0.04-0.1 um over 3-6 um EN) as the reference frame
testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets declared class; DO NOT label immersion-only product 'gold plated' (>=0.5 um) — it is flash class [FACT: nomenclature rules exist in jewelry-marking regulations, specifics per market]

testing_acceptance.test: Ni-P thickness + uniformity by XRF (multi-point incl. recesses)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: 3-8 um barrier class, recess-to-flat ratio ~1 (uniformity IS the process spec — deviation means bath fault)

testing_acceptance.standard_class: cross-section or gold-strip + SEM in industry; DIY proxy: tape-pull + solder/heat test on coupon, or nitric-swell inspection
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no spreading dark corroded Ni under stripped gold; any mud-crack pattern under the flash = reject the lot and shorten immersion dwell

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ASTM B571 class (bend on coupon, thermal quench, tape)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no flake/peel; NOTE bend test on ENIG coupons will craze the Ni-P — assess adhesion (delamination) not cracking (intrinsic)

testing_acceptance.standard_class: nitric vapor ASTM B735 class / artificial sweat spot
testing_acceptance.acceptance: immersion flash is intrinsically porous at <0.15 um — acceptance must be set per product exposure class, or the EN layer declared the corrosion barrier

testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 after EN 12472 simulated wear [FACT: regulation]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: 0.5 ug/cm2/week articles / 0.2 piercing — with 0.1 um gold over Ni-P, expect this to be the FAILING test for jewelry unless gold is built up; send-out lab before EU sales

testing_acceptance.standard_class: XRF or supplier analysis; microhardness ASTM B578 class
testing_acceptance.acceptance: P in declared band (mid-phos 6-9%); hardness in as-plated class window — drift signals bath aging past MTO
uniform gilt, no ghost patches (skip plating), no pink/grey read-through

defects_and_remedies.defect: black pad class failure: gold looks fine, coating fails adhesion/corrodes at Ni-Au interface, mud-cracked dark Ni-P under stripped gold
defects_and_remedies.cause: hyper-corrosion of Ni-P grain boundaries by an over-aggressive or over-long immersion gold step (bath too hot, pH low, dwell too long, Ni-P P-content low or bath-aged)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: shorten dwell to plateau time only, run neutral-type immersion gold, keep EN bath inside MTO limit and P in mid/high band; scrap affected parts — it cannot be fixed on the part [FACT: canonical ENIG failure mode]

defects_and_remedies.defect: EN bath crash: entire bath turns grey/black, plates the tank, sponge Ni everywhere, bath dead in minutes
defects_and_remedies.cause: metastable bath nucleated — particles, Pd drag-in, overheated spot on heater, stabilizer depleted, loading too low
defects_and_remedies.remedy: prevention only: continuous filtration, water-bath heating, rinse after activation, keep loading in window, stabilizer per TDS; crashed bath = dump, nitric-strip the tank, remake

defects_and_remedies.defect: skip plating / bald patches in EN
defects_and_remedies.cause: grease, passive stainless, failed sensitize/activate on non-conductor, stabilizer excess (over-poisoned edges)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: re-run pretreatment; verify water-break; refresh activator; cut stabilizer dosing

defects_and_remedies.defect: pale, ghostly or patchy immersion gold
defects_and_remedies.cause: Au content low, T low, dwell short of plateau, or Ni-P surface passivated (slow transfer)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: feed Au to setpoint, hold 80-85 C, wet-transfer within a minute, dwell to plateau — but NOT beyond (black pad trade-off)

defects_and_remedies.defect: immersion gold bath slows then quits despite Au in spec
defects_and_remedies.cause: accumulated Ni2+ past tolerance (the displacement byproduct) — end of bath life
defects_and_remedies.remedy: dump to precious-metal reclaimer, remake; extend next life with better post-EN rinsing

defects_and_remedies.defect: autocatalytic gold bath plates the tank/filter instead of the parts
defects_and_remedies.cause: reducer-driven homogeneous nucleation — dust, scratches, overfeed of reducer, temperature spike
defects_and_remedies.remedy: small lidded tank, continuous fine filtration, feed reducer in small scheduled doses, polish/passivate tank; accept short bath life as intrinsic

defects_and_remedies.defect: gold flash wears through to grey Ni-P in days-to-weeks of wear
defects_and_remedies.cause: not a fault — physics: 0.05-0.1 um of soft gold has near-zero wear budget
defects_and_remedies.remedy: product design decision: autocatalytic or electrolytic gold build to >=0.5-2.5 um for anything worn; or sell as 'gold flash' honestly

defects_and_remedies.defect: coated part cracks/flakes when bent or hammered
defects_and_remedies.remedy: none at the coating level; form first, coat second (this family's geometry-independence makes form-first painless)

defects_and_remedies.defect: dull, dark or rough EN deposit; rate falling
defects_and_remedies.cause: bath past MTO (orthophosphite ballast), pH drifted low, T low, metallic contamination
defects_and_remedies.remedy: correct pH/T; if MTO >4-8, dump and remake — no additive rescues an orthophosphite-saturated bath [FACT: standard EN limitation]

defects_and_remedies.defect: gas pits / vertical streaks on EN
defects_and_remedies.cause: H2 bubbles clinging to upward-facing or sheltered surfaces
defects_and_remedies.remedy: rock/rotate parts, improve solution movement, orient critical faces vertically

cost_drivers: EN bath as a scheduled consumable: MTO-limited life (4-8 turnovers) means chemistry cost recurs with throughput, unlike a long-lived Watts tank
energy: two baths held at 85-91 C (EN) and 75-90 C (Au) — the highest sustained heat load of any family in this factory

gold inventory small (0.5-2 g/L in a 1-2 L bath = 1-4 g Au) — the CHEAPEST gold-bath entry ticket of all routes, because immersion baths are lean and small [ESTIMATE: arithmetic on published ranges, high]
gold per piece tiny at immersion thickness (~5 cm2 ring at 0.08 um ≈ 0.8 mg Au) — but the product is then flash-class, not wear-class; autocatalytic build erases the saving at 1-3 um/h slowness
immersion-Au bath death by Ni accumulation — rinse discipline is literally bath-life money
Pd activator (for non-conductors): palladium is a precious metal; per-piece Pd cost is small but the made-up activator ages
autocatalytic gold: short bath life + slow rate = highest cost per gold micron in the factory; use only where rectifier-free thickness is non-negotiable
no rectifier, no anodes, no racks-with-contacts: genuine capex saving vs electroplating
labor profile: less fixturing skill, more bath-babysitting (T, pH, MTO, filtration)
testing: XRF service, EN 1811 send-out (expect failures at flash thickness), black-pad screening on any ENIG-style lot

hazards: nickel sulfate and Ni-P surfaces: Carc. 2 class, skin sensitizer Cat 1 — the #1 contact allergen; aquatic-toxic [FACT]
lead-acetate-class EN stabilizers: Repr. 1A cumulative toxin (choose Pb-free EN products) [FACT]
KAu(CN)2 in cyanide-type immersion/autocatalytic golds: acutely toxic cyanide salt; classic autocatalytic bath adds FREE KCN — HCN liberation on acid contact; strict acid segregation [FACT]
borohydride reducers: water-reactive, H2 evolution; DMAB acutely toxic; hydrazine-class reducers Carc. 1B [FACT]
sulfite/thiosulfate CN-free baths: SO2 gas on acid contact [FACT]
hot baths at ~90 C: scald hazard, hot corrosive splash; hot ammonia additions to EN release NH3 vapor [FACT]
SnCl2/HCl and PdCl2 activators: corrosive/irritant class [FACT]
hypophosphite: low hazard in use; phosphine only under strong-oxidizer abuse [FACT]
controls: choose the CN-FREE immersion gold + Pb-FREE EN product pair for any residential/DIY line — this drops the two worst hazard tiers of the family at small performance cost
acid/gold segregation discipline regardless of chemistry (HCN in CN-type, SO2 in CN-free — same rule, different gas)
water-bath (indirect) heating: eliminates heater hot-spot bath crashes AND bare-element scald/fire risk
ventilation over hot tanks (NH3, aerosols); lids between uses
nitrile gloves + goggles + apron; nickel-allergic persons should not run this line at all (sensitizer exposure is chronic, not acute)
buy commercial EN + immersion gold systems with TDS/SDS; do not self-compound; never improvise reducers into gold baths

spent EN bath is Ni-rich aquatic-toxic waste: to licensed disposal, never drain; spent gold baths to precious-metal reclaimer (asset); Pd activator waste collected separately; local discharge rules [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check]
safety.waste: Three streams, keep separate: (1) spent EN (Ni + orthophosphite, regulated, recurring because of MTO life) — the volume driver; (2) gold-bearing spent immersion/electroless gold and drag-out — small, valuable, to reclaimer; (3) Sn/Pd activator residues — small, Pd has reclaim value. CN-type golds additionally need cyanide-waste handling; the CN-free pairing keeps the whole family's waste profile to 'regulated but mild'.

diy_feasibility.verdict: YES for its NICHE, NO as the main jewelry finish. Feasible at kitchen-lab scale with commercial Pb-free EN + CN-free immersion gold kits and zero electrical hardware — arguably the lowest-capex way to put real gold color on metal. But the displacement ceiling is physics: ~0.1 um is flash, not jewelry wear plate, and the Ni-P underlayer forbids plate-then-form entirely. Its honest roles in the owner's factory: (1) METALLIZATION FRONT-END for glass/ceramic houseware (sensitize -> activate -> EN -> then ELECTROplate gold from the sibling files); (2) uniform barrier + gold seed on complex/hollow/filigree formed pieces that electroplating reaches poorly; (3) budget 'gold flash' product tier sold honestly. Autocatalytic thick gold exists but is the slowest, fussiest, costliest gold per micron — for wire jewelry the sibling electroplating routes win on every axis once a rectifier is owned.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: 2-5 L Pb-free mid-phos EN kit (bath + replenisher pair) in glass/PP vessel in a water bath, 0.5-2 L CN-free immersion gold kit likewise, thermometer + calibrated pH meter, PP baskets, 1-5 um filter loop for the EN, dilute-ammonia pH feed, SnCl2 + PdCl2 (or one-step colloid) activator set only if non-conductors are in scope, drag-out jars, MTO logbook, XRF via service lab. No rectifier, no anodes. Gold-in-bath entry cost 1-4 g Au — the cheapest gold entry in the factory. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on component list, no invented prices]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: immersion thickness ceiling ~0.1-0.15 um is mechanistic and cannot be tuned past; Ni-P brittleness bans post-coat forming; EN bath dies on schedule (MTO) no matter the care; EN 1811 nickel-release compliance at flash gold thickness is unlikely for EU skin-contact jewelry without gold build-up; food-contact drinkware with Ni-P + trace stabilizers [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check]; classic KCN/borohydride autocatalytic gold is out of bounds for a residential shop on hazard class alone; glass adhesion depends on roughening/etch quality — the DIY-safe etch options are the weak link [ESTIMATE: practice-based, medium]
